commit.subject: LU-20510 osc: wait for OST_SYNC issued on the fsync error path
commit.message:
LU-20510 osc: wait for OST_SYNC issued on the fsync error path

osc_io_fsync_start() issues the asynchronous OST_SYNC RPC unconditionally
via osc_fsync_ost(), but only records that it is in flight when no earlier
error has been latched:

	rc = osc_fsync_ost(env, osc, fio);
	if (result == 0) {
		cbargs->opc_rpc_sent = 1;
		result = rc;
	}

osc_io_fsync_end() waits only when opc_rpc_sent is set, so once
osc_cache_writeback_range() or osc_cache_wait_range() has failed, the io is
torn down with the RPC still in flight. Its completion then runs
osc_async_upcall() on &oio->oi_cbarg, which lives inside struct osc_session
-- memory already returned to osc_session_kmem. The resulting freelist
corruption surfaces later, at an unrelated allocation, typically as:

  general protection fault: 0000 [#1] SMP DEBUG_PAGEALLOC
  RIP: 0010:memset_erms+0x9/0x10
   kmem_cache_alloc+0x307/0x430
   osc_session_init+0x31/0x150 [osc]
   cl_env_new+0x223/0x2e0 [obdclass]
   cl_env_get+0xe3/0x3a0 [obdclass]

The window is normally unreachable, since nothing fails writeback on a
healthy client, but it opens on OST I/O errors or client eviction, and
CL_FSYNC_RECLAIM makes it reachable from background reclaim writeback.

Record the RPC as in flight whenever it was actually sent, regardless of any
previously latched error, so osc_io_fsync_end() always waits for it.

Verified on a slab-debug kernel with writeback-error injection: without this
patch 6 of 13 runs crashed, with the crash occurring in exactly the runs that
entered the window; with it, 0 of 10 runs crashed while 5 still entered the
same window.

Fixes: 8aa231a99468 ("LU-16713 llite: writeback/commit pages under memory pressure")
